title: Vietjet: Ho Chi Minh City Direct Return Perth $335, Sydney $434, Melbourne $438, Brisbane $447 @ IWantThatFlight
body:
Deal: Vietjet: Ho Chi Minh City Direct Return Perth $335, Sydney $434, Melbourne $438, Brisbane $447 @ IWantThatFlight

[TonyBaloney] thanks and confirming that this is out of Sydney International and not the newly announced WSI airport that Vietjet are flying out of still?
[IWantThatFlight] Yes, flights are out of Sydney International
[TonyBaloney] Thanks and just saw a news announcement of 20% off for this week only on WSI flights too! will be intetersting too see if even cheaper than this!?
[KanTakahashi] 8/8 deals earlier was 30% off (bundle pkg), and they're running $0/discount deals quite often.
20% code is the same for all routes - WSI/SYD/MEL/PER, the price from WSI is ~$75-80 cheaper if you're keen to fly out from there ($228.30, normal discounted price out of SYD around $310) but not a lot of dates for now.
[asdert000] Went in May, picked a flight that landed at 7am, got through customs in 15 minutes.
No shit you have to wait 1-2 hours if you land at peak time. Common sense bud, happens anywhere.
[Fuzor] Yeah cause the Albaneseeee government is just a shining beacon isn't it? Australian workers continue to pay more and more tax on everything under the sun and that money does nothing before it disappears, yet you think theres no corruption?
Also you buy visas before you leave for Vietnam so there is no 2 or 3 hours wait
[zfind] I’ve had both this experience and those from other commenters. Yes it’s not that efficient but Tan Son Nhat (which is what you might be referring to) is old and doesn’t have enough capacity to deal with the explosion in tourist numbers to VN.
If you’re departing, it’s worth heeding the 2h timeframe as security can get super long. If you’re arriving who cares, just stand and wait.
Thailand also has express skip-the-line systems, not just Viet Nam. Australia is stupidly corrupt in other ways, same difference.
[justin201] Pay for Fast track service and you dont need to wait the immigration clearance. It is obvious to take a lot of time if you reach Vietnam in peak hour. Try some night or early morning flight
[MrZ] While there please visit Vietnam war memorial and pay respects to all US/Aussie soldiers who fought for freedom (and sadly lost).
[ntt] I don't think you get the right ideas the war memorial over there for
[MrZ] Well obviously there are also the south Vietnamese soldiers who fought for freedom as well. They also deserve our respect.
[zfind] The north Vietnamese were fighting for freedom too, remember them and the millions of civilians who died because America was afraid of losing influence in a region thousands of kilometres away…
[MrZ] @zfind: The North Vietnamese were fighting to "free" the South from capitalism and oppress them under a communist regime. Why didn't they care about the thoughts and feelings of the millions of already free people living in the South who wanted nothing to do with communism?
[zfind] @MrZ: Viet Nam had the right to self determination just as any other country did, but communism threatened the US worldview (hegemony) so it had to be stopped. The US rarely has acted out of altruism when it comes to global affairs and this was no exception. Just because you don’t like communism doesn’t mean others aren’t allowed to choose it. The point being, if you believe what the US did is right then you’re also fine with other bully nations imposing their rules on a weaker neighbour - many parallels of which you’ll find today. The US being involved in a war is really more of a sign it’s unfounded and a bad idea than the old glory of WW2.
I’ll add that Viet Nam’s partial embrace of communism was one of the direct outcomes of hundreds of years of brutal imperialist occupation. If that was their choice then so be it. Capitalism has turned out to be just as vile anyway.
Just because Australians died there doesn’t make it a just war. It also doesn’t stop you paying respects to them, rightly. But the loss and damage and brutality inflicted on the people of that country, of both sides deserves recognition and understanding, not just blind belief.
[MrZ] @zfind: I never said I agreed with the US involvement in the war. But think about this, what if the US didn't get involved in the Korean war, and the North Koreans won and forced communism on the South. Would you say the South would be better off under North Korea's communist rule, or how they are now?
[justin201] Saigon is Ho Chi Minh City, just the old name
